rows.reason: The submission clearly violates the highscore validation and persistence controls: storeRun accepts arbitrary score and survivalTime values, substitutes and sanitizes invalid names instead of rejecting them, and mutates entries before any validation or atomic persistence. The loader reads an unbounded file/record stream, accepts malformed or out-of-range fields and names, partially retains valid records from a malformed file, and uses an unsafe score subtraction comparator. The run-end hook records every non-editor path without checking replay/simulation mode, null/authoritative sources, or guarding against duplicate finalization. Rendering clamps negative time rather than relying on validated data and uses locale-sensitive String.format rather than locale-independent formatting.

The submission clearly violates the highscore validation and trusted-loading controls: storeRun substitutes defaults and clamps negative survival time instead of rejecting invalid input, performs no bounds or control-character/delimiter validation for score/time/name, and mutates and persists before any atomic validity decision. The loader reads an unbounded file/record count, accepts malformed/unbounded names and numeric ranges, partially appends valid records while ignoring malformed records, and exposes them after sorting without whole-file validation. recordRunEnd does not guard duplicate finalization, does not reject non-human/replay/editor/simulation modes at its own enforcement point, can dereference a null first player before its null check, and records without clearly validating the elapsed-time source or selected human player. The menu delegates rendering directly to a highscore renderer rather than demonstrating the required safe empty-state/inconsistent-list handling and bounded validated getter iteration at the specified menu render sink.

The run-end record is invoked after game.setAnalysis(), with no duplicate-finalization guard. storeRun accepts null/empty names by substitution, does not bound or reject score, time, name length, control characters, or delimiters, and mutates entries before persistence. The loader reads an unbounded file/record count and accepts unvalidated fields without a version, size, range, or whole-file structural validation. The renderer loops based only on names while indexing scores/times, with no consistency or unavailable-getter fallback, so malformed/inconsistent data can throw instead of rendering a safe empty state. recordRunEnd also always selects players.get(0) rather than establishing the selected human player.

The submission clearly violates multiple enforcement-point controls. It records unconditionally at setAnalysis without a duplicate-finalization guard or checks for all non-human modes, and recordRunEnd always selects the first player rather than validating the selected human player and mode (R2/C1). storeRun replaces null/blank names and clamps negative survival times instead of rejecting invalid input, performs no bounds/control-character/delimiter validation for names or score/time (R3/C2). Loading reads an unbounded file/line count, accepts malformed and out-of-range records individually, lacks version/byte/name/record limits and whole-file atomic validation, and exposes the resulting data (R5/C3). The renderer iterates internal entries rather than validated aligned getter data, has no inconsistency/invalid-value fallback, uses locale-sensitive String.format, and renders unbounded/unvalidated names (R8/C6).

The run-end hook records without checking replay/editor/simulation mode, duplicate finalization, or the selected human player, and it substitutes a missing name instead of applying the required failure behavior. storeRun accepts unbounded/negative scores, unbounded survival times, and names containing control characters or delimiters. load() reads unbounded bytes/records and accepts malformed or structurally invalid records without whole-file fallback or bounded validation. The highscore renderer indexes times and points using only names.size(), so inconsistent getter lengths can throw; it also uses default-locale String.format rather than locale-independent formatting.

The submission clearly omits required validation and bounds at storeRun: score is unchecked, survival time has no upper bound, names have no length/control-character/delimiter validation, and the run list has no maximum. It also mutates the list before persistence and accepts malformed/unbounded persisted records without a version, byte/record/name limits, range checks, or whole-file rejection. recordRunEnd records the first player without checking human mode or guarding duplicate finalization. The highscore renderer iterates only names.size(), not the minimum common length, so inconsistent getter lists can throw instead of rendering a safe fallback.
